labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes' compression feasibility check can misjudge local/hosted Ollama auxiliary compression models because it may trust configured/model-advertised context lengths instead of the model's effective runtime context.

The result is a **false-safe / misleading compression warning path**:
- Hermes may decide the compression model is large enough and suppress the warning.
- The real Ollama runtime may still be capped lower (for example by server/runtime defaults or `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`).
- Compression then runs against a smaller real window than Hermes believes it has.

## Why this matters

This is not just cosmetic. It can make the user think compression is safely configured when the auxiliary compression model can still truncate or degrade the summarisation prompt at runtime.

## Observed evidence

From a live Hermes + Ollama setup on `mac-ai-server`:

- Hermes emitted:
  - `Compression model qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_0 (ollama) context is 32,768 tokens, but the main model gpt-5.4 (openai-codex)'s compression threshold was 231,200 tokens. Auto-lowered this session's threshold to 32,768 tokens so compression can run.`
- Local Hermes config had optimistic Ollama entries such as:
  - `providers.ollama.models.qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_0.context_length: 131072`
  - `extra_body.num_ctx: 131072`
- Live Ollama model metadata from `/api/show` reported:
  - `qwen2.context_length: 32768` for `qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_0`
  - `qwen2.context_length: 32768` for `qwen2.5-coder:7b-instruct-q4_0`
- The Ollama launchd environment on the host also contained a global:
  - `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=131072`

So there are at least three competing sources of truth:
1. Hermes provider config / `config_context_length`
2. Ollama model metadata (`/api/show`)
3. Ollama runtime/server-level context controls (`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`, runtime `num_ctx` behavior)

## Suspected root cause

`agent/conversation_compression.py::check_compression_model_feasibility()` resolves `aux_context` via `get_model_context_length(...)`.

The likely problem is that this path can treat one of the *advertised* values as authoritative instead of the *effective runtime* context the auxiliary Ollama request will actually get.

That becomes risky when:
- `auxiliary.compression.context_length` is set manually and too high
- `providers.ollama.models.<model>.context_length` overstates reality
- Ollama runtime constraints differ from model metadata
- a server-level/default context setting changes effective runtime behavior

In short: the feasibility check appears vulnerable to **context-source drift** on local Ollama.

## Likely user impact

- misleading or suppressed compression warnings
- false confidence that compression is safe
- auxiliary compression requests running with a smaller real context than Hermes expects
- degraded summaries / truncation instead of a clear warning

## Candidate fix directions

1. Prefer the **effective runtime context** for Ollama feasibility checks, not just configured/model-advertised context.
2. Treat `config_context_length` as an override with suspicion unless it matches a runtime probe.
3. If Hermes cannot verify the real runtime window for Ollama, fail conservative and warn.
4. Align the auxiliary compression path with whatever runtime context enforcement already exists for the main Ollama model path.

## Related code surface

- `agent/conversation_compression.py`
- `agent/model_metadata.py`
- any Ollama-specific context-resolution / runtime `num_ctx` handling used by the main model path

## Agent review notes

A Claude Code review of the relevant code path concluded this is worth filing as a real bug because the feasibility check can create a false-safe state for local Ollama auxiliary compression models when configured/provider metadata overstates the real runtime context.

A Codex review independently agreed on the same failure mode: context advertised by config/model metadata can overstate the usable runtime context, especially when Ollama runtime settings diverge.

## Suggested title

Compression feasibility check trusts Ollama-advertised context over effective runtime context, causing false-safe auxiliary compression decisions

items.body:
[Bug]: Session store prunes sessions with live background processes when the active-process check raises (orphans running work)

## Summary
`SessionStore.prune_old_entries` is supposed to keep any session that still has a live background process attached, so long-running background work isn't orphaned. But when the `has_active_processes_fn` callback *raises*, the exception is swallowed at `debug` level and execution falls through to the age check — so the session gets pruned anyway, silently killing the record of live background work.

This directly contradicts the function's own docstring, which promises such sessions "are also kept so long-running background work isn't orphaned."

## Why it matters
- The hourly session-expiry sweep is **on by default** — `session_store_max_age_days` defaults to 90 (`test_session_store_max_age_days_defaults_to_90`), so this path runs unconditionally for essentially every install.
- The failure is **fail-open on a destructive operation**: any transient error in the active-process probe (e.g. the process-registry lookup momentarily raising) causes irreversible pruning of a session that owns running background work. The user loses the ability to resume/track that work.
- It is **silent** — logged only at `debug`, so operators get no signal that live work was orphaned.
- Background processes are an actively-used, load-bearing feature (see related routing bugs #52447), so the blast radius is real, not theoretical.

## Root cause
`gateway/session.py`, `prune_old_entries` (currently ~lines 2172-2182 on `main`):

```python
if self._has_active_processes_fn is not None:
    try:
        if self._has_active_processes_fn(entry.session_key):
            continue
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.debug(
            "has_active_processes_fn raised during prune for %s: %s",
            entry.session_key, exc,
        )
if entry.updated_at < cutoff:      # <-- falls through to here on raise, prunes anyway
    removed_keys.append(key)
```

There is no `continue` after the `except`, so a raised active-process check does not protect the entry.

## Reproduction
1. Have a session older than `session_store_max_age_days` (default 90d) that owns a live background process.
2. Make `has_active_processes_fn` raise for that session key (e.g. transient failure in the process-registry lookup).
3. Trigger the prune sweep (or wait for the hourly watcher).
4. **Observed:** the session is pruned despite the live process. **Expected:** the session is kept (fail-safe) because we could not confirm it was idle.

## Proposed fix
Add a fail-safe `continue` inside the `except` so an indeterminate active-process check keeps the entry:

```python
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.debug(
            "has_active_processes_fn raised during prune for %s: %s",
            entry.session_key, exc,
        )
        continue   # fail safe: can't confirm idle → keep, don't orphan live work
```

One-line change plus tests covering both paths (raise → kept; returns False → pruned).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When `has_active_processes_fn` raises during prune, the entry is retained (not added to `removed_keys`).
- [ ] Normal pruning is unchanged: an old entry whose active-process check returns `False` is still pruned.
- [ ] Regression test covering both paths in `tests/gateway/test_session_store_prune.py`.

## Related (do not merge into this fix)
- #52447 background-process notification routing (confirms background processes are load-bearing) — separate bug.
- Follow-up: two other unguarded `has_active_processes_fn` call sites (`_is_session_expired`, `_should_reset`) fail *closed* and stall a whole watcher tick — lower severity, file separately.

items.title: [Bug]: Compression lock fails OPEN on any acquisition error — concurrent compression can fork the session

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
[Bug]: Compression lock fails OPEN on any acquisition error — concurrent compression can fork the session

## Summary
When acquiring the per-session compression lock, `agent/conversation_compression.py` catches **all** exceptions with a single broad `except Exception` and treats every failure as "no lock subsystem present," setting `_lock_acquired = True` and proceeding with compression anyway. The intent was to tolerate one specific case — a version-skewed `SessionDB` that structurally lacks the lock method — but as written it also fails open on *transient/anomalous* errors from a lock subsystem that genuinely exists. In that case two compactors can run concurrently on the same session and **fork it**.

## Why it matters
- The lock exists specifically to prevent concurrent compression from forking a session. Failing open on a real-but-erroring lock defeats the guard exactly when it's needed.
- Session fork = corrupted/duplicated conversation state — user-visible and not self-healing.
- This is the failure mode the existing flaky test `test_concurrent_compression_does_not_fork_session` guards against (see #52526); the fail-open path is a plausible root cause of that flake.

## Root cause
`agent/conversation_compression.py` (currently ~lines 565-585 on `main`):

```python
try:
    _lock_acquired = _lock_db.try_acquire_compression_lock(
        _lock_sid, _lock_holder, ttl_seconds=_lock_ttl
    )
except Exception as _lock_err:
    # Broken/absent lock subsystem (version skew, etc.). Proceed WITHOUT the lock.
    _lock_holder = None
    ...
    _lock_acquired = True  # <-- fails OPEN for EVERY exception, incl. transient
```

The DB layer (`hermes_state.py`) already catches `sqlite3.Error` internally and returns `False`, so contention does *not* reach here — anything that does reach this `except` is a genuine anomaly, yet it's treated as "no lock, proceed."

## Proposed fix
Split the handler by exception class:
- `except (AttributeError, TypeError)` → **fail open** (structural absence / version skew — the method is missing, or its signature predates the `ttl_seconds=` kwarg and raises unexpected-keyword `TypeError`). This preserves the original #34475 rationale. *(Both AttributeError and TypeError are needed: since `ttl_seconds=` was added to the call, a stale `SessionDB` now raises `TypeError`, not `AttributeError`.)*
- `except Exception` → **fail closed** (`_lock_acquired = False`): skip compression this cycle and retry next, rather than risk a concurrent-compression fork.

The existing `if not _lock_acquired:` branch already skips compression safely.

## Reproduction
1. Make `try_acquire_compression_lock` raise a generic error that is not `sqlite3.Error` (a present-but-erroring lock subsystem), e.g. `RuntimeError`.
2. Trigger auto-compression.
3. **Observed:** compression proceeds unlocked (`_lock_acquired = True`); a concurrent compactor can fork the session. **Expected:** compression is skipped this cycle and retried.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A generic `Exception` from lock acquisition results in `_lock_acquired = False` and compression is skipped this cycle (no fork).
- [ ] An `AttributeError`/`TypeError` (version skew) still fails open and proceeds (backward-compatible with #34475).
- [ ] Existing tests in `tests/agent/test_compression_concurrent_fork.py` still pass; new tests cover both branches.

## Related (do not merge into this fix)
- #52526 flaky `test_concurrent_compression_does_not_fork_session` — likely improved by this fix; verify separately.
- #57631 misleading "No changes from compression" when lock is held — separate UX follow-up.
- #57771 / #53008 / #58630 / #58407 / #58745 — unrelated compression-loop/threshold bugs; do not bundle.

### Bug Description

- `config.yaml` has `terminal.backend: docker` with proper docker volumes (`/home:/home:ro` etc.)
- hermes serve (the headless backend used by the Desktop app) never calls `apply_terminal_config_to_env()` for its own process environment
- Therefore `TERMINAL_ENV` is never set, terminal tool always runs in local mode
- The config bridge only applies to child processes (TUI, dashboard PTY), never to the serve process itself

Fix: Add `apply_terminal_config_to_env()` to `start_server()` in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` before the server starts accepting tool calls.

Workaround: Set `TERMINAL_ENV=docker` in `~/.hermes/.env` manually.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure terminal.backend: docker in ~/.hermes/config.yaml with proper Docker volumes:

```
terminal:
  backend: docker
  docker_image: hermes-sandbox:latest
  docker_volumes:
    - /home:/home:ro
  container_persistent: true
```

2. Launch the Hermes Desktop app (hermes desktop)
3. Disabled File Operations and Code Execution in Hermes Desktop
4. /reset desktop and desktop still bypass docker modify files in /home directly

### Expected Behavior

`TERMINAL_ENV` should be set to docker automatically from `config.yaml`, and terminal commands should execute inside the Docker sandbox container.

### Actual Behavior

Despite terminal.backend: docker in config.yaml, the Desktop app's serve process never sets TERMINAL_ENV, so the terminal tool runs in local mode. All shell commands execute directly on the host, bypassing the Docker sandbox entirely:

```
# Inside a terminal() call from the Desktop app:
systemd-detect-virt → "none"           # not in any container
cat /proc/1/cgroup → Chromium scope    # running on host as Electron child
```

This means:
- docker_volumes with :ro is never applied — Docker is never invoked
- The agent can modify files in /home directly with no sandbox protection
- container_cpu, container_memory, container_disk limits are ignored
- The sandbox isolation the user configured is completely bypassed

The config says backend: docker but the Desktop acts as if it's backend: local.

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

Ubuntu 26.04

`start_server()` in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` does not call `apply_terminal_config_to_env()` for its own process environment before accepting tool calls. The fix is adding at the beginning of `start_server()`:

items.title: delegate_task broken in cron sessions since 0.18.2: forced background=true prevents subagent results from returning

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## What happened

delegate_task was working correctly in cron jobs from 7/1 through 7/8 (v0.18.1). After upgrading to 0.18.2 on 7/9, all delegate_task calls from cron agents became fire-and-forget — returning only a 300-char dispatch confirmation instead of waiting for the actual subagent results (1000-23000 chars of analysis).

## Evidence (from agent.log)

Before 0.18.2 (7/1-7/8):
```
delegate_task completed (35.42s, 3,419 chars)  ✓ sync, real results
delegate_task completed (402.71s, 15,075 chars) ✓ sync, real results
```

After 0.18.2 (7/9+):
```
Dispatched async delegation batch deleg_xxx
delegate_task completed (0.05s, 322 chars)  ✗ async, dispatch confirm only
```

## Root cause

`run_agent._dispatch_delegate_task` (line 5685) forces `background=True` for all top-level agents:

```python
_is_subagent = getattr(self, "_delegate_depth", 0) > 0
return _delegate_task(
    ...
    background=(not _is_subagent),  # top-level → always async
)
```

In interactive sessions this is fine — async results re-enter the conversation. But cron sessions produce ONE final response and exit. The subagent results never arrive because the session is already closed.

## Impact

Any cron job that uses delegate_task silently produces incomplete output. The agent dispatches subagents, gets back "dispatched" confirmations, then outputs its final response — which contains only placeholder text like "waiting for results" instead of actual analysis.

This affects the evening portfolio report cron (6-role investment committee) and any other scheduled job that relies on parallel subagent analysis.

## Suggested fix

Detect cron/stateless session context and fall back to synchronous execution (inline the subagent results), similar to how the stateless HTTP API path already falls back at lines 2778-2796:

```python
if not _async_ok:
    # ... run synchronously instead
```

A cron session is effectively stateless — it should get the same treatment.

## Workaround

Currently working around by removing delegate_task from cron prompts entirely and having the main agent simulate multiple analyst roles in its own context. This loses the benefit of isolated subagent contexts and adds significant prompt complexity.

items.title: False-positive "Stale systemd unit" warning: timing check reads synthesized defaults from `systemctl --user` for system-scope units

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

`gateway/shutdown_forensics.py::check_systemd_timing_alignment` queries the **user** systemd manager before the system one:

```python
# Query systemctl for TimeoutStopUSec. ... Try user first since
# that's the common case for hermes.
for flag in (["--user"], []):
```

When the gateway is installed as a **system** unit (`hermes gateway install`), the user manager has never loaded `hermes-gateway.service` — but `systemctl --user show <unit> --property=TimeoutStopUSec` still **exits 0** and returns **synthesized default properties** for the unloaded unit. On distros whose user-manager default is low (Arch family: `DefaultTimeoutStopUSec=10s`), the loop accepts that value and never consults the system manager.

Result: every gateway start logs a stale-unit warning with a phantom `TimeoutStopSec=10s`, even when the real unit is correct — and re-running the suggested `hermes gateway install --force` can never clear it.

## Reproduction (hermes-agent 0.18.2, system-scope unit, Arch-family distro)

```console
$ systemctl --user show hermes-gateway.service --property=TimeoutStopUSec; echo rc=$?
TimeoutStopUSec=10s
rc=0
$ systemctl show hermes-gateway.service --property=TimeoutStopUSec
TimeoutStopUSec=3min 30s
$ systemctl --user show --property=DefaultTimeoutStopUSec
DefaultTimeoutStopUSec=10s
$ grep TimeoutStopSec /etc/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service
TimeoutStopSec=210
```

Journal on every start, despite the correct unit:

```
WARNING gateway.run: Stale systemd unit detected: hermes-gateway.service has TimeoutStopSec=10s but drain_timeout=180s (expected >=210s). systemd may SIGKILL the gateway mid-drain. Run `hermes gateway install --force` to regenerate the unit, or shorten agent.restart_drain_timeout.
```

## Suggested fix

Request `LoadState` together with the timeout and skip any scope that reports `not-found`:

```python
["systemctl", *flag, "show", unit_name,
 "--property=TimeoutStopUSec", "--property=LoadState"]
# ... skip this scope if LoadState=not-found
```

(Alternatively: prefer the system scope when running under the system manager — e.g. `INVOCATION_ID` present and no user bus.)

## Related

`hermes gateway install --force`, when run via `sudo` from a session without a user bus, crashes at its final step with `CalledProcessError: Command '['systemctl', '--user', 'daemon-reload']' returned non-zero exit status 1` — after having already written the system unit successfully. Same scope-assumption family; a guard (skip `--user` reload when the user bus is absent, or treat it as best-effort) would make the install path clean under sudo.

items.title: [Bug]: delegate_task results are lost when called from Kanban workers; parent exits even with goal_mode

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

A dispatcher-spawned Kanban worker can call `delegate_task`, receive a background handle immediately, then finish its turn and exit before the delegated result is delivered. The Kanban card remains `running` because the parent correctly did not call `kanban_complete` before receiving the review verdict. The dispatcher later sees a dead worker and records `crashed` or `protocol_violation`.

Enabling `goal_mode` does not prevent this failure: in the observed run, no goal-judge result or continuation turn occurred after the worker's final response.

This makes `delegate_task` unsafe inside one-shot Kanban workers for required review/verification work. The result is both lost work and a misleading worker-lifecycle failure.

### Observed Incident

Environment:

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), upstream `7b5ba205`
- Linux, Python 3.11.15
- Dispatcher-spawned Kanban worker
- `goal_mode: true`
- `goal_max_turns: 60`

Sequence:

1. The Kanban worker completed a substantial implementation and its verification suite successfully.
2. It called `delegate_task` for a required independent review.
3. `delegate_task` returned a delegation handle immediately; the parent continued rather than waiting.
4. The parent emitted a normal final response stating that the review remained in progress.
5. The parent process exited while the Kanban task was still `running` and without calling `kanban_complete`/`kanban_block`—correctly, because the required review had not returned.
6. The delegated review never produced a completion message, persisted summary, or verdict in the parent session.
7. No goal judge or goal continuation turn ran despite goal mode being enabled.
8. The dispatcher later observed the dead PID and recorded the run as `crashed` (or `protocol_violation` when the clean exit code is retained), consuming retry budget and eventually blocking the card.

There was no implementation failure, test failure, provider error, traceback, or iteration-budget exhaustion in this run.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Kanban card with `goal_mode=true` and a nontrivial `goal_max_turns`.
2. Instruct the worker to:
   - perform implementation work;
   - call `delegate_task` for a required independent review;
   - complete the card only after receiving and triaging the review result.
3. Let the implementation finish and the worker dispatch the review.
4. Observe that `delegate_task` returns immediately and the worker can emit a final text response while the child is still running.
5. Observe that the worker process exits, the child result is never inserted into the now-dead parent session, and the Kanban task remains `running`.
6. On the next dispatcher reconciliation, observe `crashed`/`protocol_violation` and retry-budget consumption.
7. Inspect the session/task history: goal mode did not judge or continue the turn.

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should not allow a Kanban worker to silently enter a lifecycle state where required delegated work is pending but the parent process can exit.

One of these contracts would be valid:

1. Keep the Kanban parent alive and route the delegation completion back as a continuation turn before allowing it to exit.
2. Drain/wait for outstanding delegations before finalizing a one-shot Kanban worker turn.
3. Reject `delegate_task` from dispatcher-spawned Kanban workers with an actionable error directing users to durable child Kanban tickets.
4. At minimum, make `async_delivery_supported()` return false for this surface and use a genuinely synchronous delegation path if one exists.

When `goal_mode` is enabled, a normal text response with unresolved delegated work should also reach the goal judge/continuation loop rather than terminating the process silently.

### Actual Behavior

- `delegate_task` returns immediately.
- Parent worker exits while child work remains pending.
- Child result is lost because the parent session/process no longer exists.
- Goal mode does not continue the worker.
- Dispatcher classifies the still-running card as a crash/protocol violation.

### Root Cause Hypothesis

This appears to be the Kanban analogue of #53027: async delegation is enabled on a finite, one-shot execution surface that does not have a durable completion-queue drain after the parent turn/process exits.

The lifecycle mismatch is:

```text
Kanban worker process lifetime < delegated child lifetime
```

while delegation delivery assumes the parent session remains available.

### Suggested Fix

- Treat dispatcher-spawned Kanban workers as unsupported for fire-and-forget delegation unless the worker runtime owns a completion-queue drain and continuation loop.
- Track outstanding delegation handles in the worker lifecycle and prevent clean process exit while required completions are pending.
- Ensure goal-mode judging/continuation runs after a text response even when delegation has been dispatched.
- If durable integration is out of scope, remove or hard-disable `delegate_task` from Kanban workers and direct agents to create dependency-gated child Kanban tickets instead.
- Add an end-to-end regression test: Kanban worker → `delegate_task` → delayed child completion → result delivered → parent continues → explicit `kanban_complete`.

### Related Issues

- #53027 — async delegation completion events lost in cron jobs (same finite-surface/queue-drain shape)
- #54566 — background `delegate_task` work is not durable when the parent exits
- #56647 — delegated children inherit Kanban lifecycle tools and can complete/block the parent's card (different failure, same unsafe Kanban/delegation boundary)
- #46706 — goal mode is not an independent completion gate

### Affected Component

Kanban worker lifecycle / `delegate_task` async delivery / goal-mode continuation

items.title: search_files silently returns 0 results on Windows when passed an absolute path (rg + MSYS_NO_PATHCONV conflict)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
**Repo:** NousResearch/hermes-agent
**Tested at commit:** `9a15fad0d` (2026-07-12) — includes the #61915 merge (`04ca34b5f`)
**Platform:** Windows 11, Git Bash (Git for Windows), ripgrep 15.1.0 (native win32 build, on PATH)

## Not a duplicate of #61915

This reproduces on a checkout that already contains #61915 ("resolve MSYS paths in file tools on Windows", merged 2026-07-10). That PR fixes the **inbound** direction — normalizing `/c/...` → `C:\...` when resolving a path in `_resolve_path_for_task` / `_resolve_base_dir` (`tools/file_tools.py`). The bug below is in the **outbound** direction — `_escape_shell_arg` rewriting `C:/...` → `/c/...` immediately before the path is handed to native `rg.exe` in `tools/file_operations.py`. Different file, different function, opposite conversion; #61915 does not touch the ripgrep command construction, so the defect survives it.

## Summary

On Windows, the `search_files` tool (and content `search` when a path is given) always returns `{"total_count": 0}` for any explicit drive-qualified path (e.g. `C:/Users/<user>/Documents/Obsidian Vault`), even though the directory exists and contains matching files. No error is surfaced — the agent believes the directory is empty and typically retriggers the same search or falls back to `terminal` + `ls`.

## Root cause

Two Windows workarounds in the codebase conflict:

1. `FileOperations._escape_shell_arg` (`tools/file_operations.py`) intentionally converts native Windows paths to MSYS form before embedding them in the shell command: `C:/Users/<user>` → `/c/Users/<user>` (via `_windows_to_msys_path`). This is correct for MSYS binaries (`ls`, `find`, `grep`) and for bash builtins like `cd`.

2. `_apply_windows_msys_bash_env_defaults` (`tools/environments/local.py`, refs #56700 / #56147) sets `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` and `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*` in every bash subprocess to stop Git Bash from mangling flags like `tasklist /FO`.

The combination breaks native Windows executables: `rg.exe` receives the literal argument `/c/Users/<user>/...` (the env vars disable the MSYS layer that would translate it back), resolves it as `<cwd-drive>:\c\Users\<user>\...`, and fails with:

```
rg: /c/Users/<user>/Documents/Obsidian Vault: IO error ... The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)
```

In `_search_files_rg` the command redirects `2>/dev/null`, so the error is swallowed and an empty (successful-looking) `SearchResult` is returned.

## Reproduction

In any Hermes bash environment on Windows (or manually, with the same env):

```bash
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'

# What search_files builds today — fails silently:
rg --files -g '*.md' '/c/Users/<user>/Documents/Obsidian Vault' 2>/dev/null   # → no output

# Same env, native path form — works:
rg --files -g '*.md' 'C:/Users/<user>/Documents/Obsidian Vault'              # → lists files
```

Via the agent: invoke `search_files` with `{"pattern": "*.md", "target": "files", "path": "C:/Users/<user>/Documents/<any existing dir>"}` → `{"total_count": 0}`.

Note the misleading interplay: calling `search_files` **without** a `path` (defaults to `.`) works, because a relative path never goes through `_windows_to_msys_path`. This makes the bug look intermittent.

## Affected call sites (all in `tools/file_operations.py`)

- `_search_files_rg` — both the `--sortr=modified` command and the plain fallback pass `self._escape_shell_arg(path)` to native `rg`.
- `_search_with_rg` — `cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(path))`.

The `find`/`grep` fallbacks are unaffected (MSYS binaries understand `/c/...` regardless of argv conversion), which also means Windows machines **without** ripgrep don't reproduce this — only ones where `rg` is installed and preferred.

## Suggested fix

For arguments destined for native Windows executables, escape without MSYS translation — pass the drive-qualified form with forward slashes, which `rg` accepts on Windows:

```python
def _escape_shell_arg_native(self, arg: str) -> str:
    """Escape a path for a NATIVE Windows executable (e.g. rg).

    Hermes disables MSYS argv path conversion in its bash subprocesses
    (MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 / MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*), so a native binary
    receives arguments verbatim. The MSYS form /c/Users/<user> produced by
    _escape_shell_arg is never translated back and resolves as
    <drive>:\c\Users\<user> — silently matching nothing. Native tools accept
    C:/Users/<user>, so pass that through untranslated. No-op for POSIX paths.
    """
    arg = arg.replace('\\', '/')
    return "'" + arg.replace("'", "'\"'\"'") + "'"
```

and use it for the `path` argument at the three `rg` call sites above (glob patterns and regex patterns can keep the existing escaping; they are not drive-qualified paths).

Verified locally: with this change, `search_files` with an explicit absolute Windows path returns correct results, and `search` (content mode) also works against absolute paths; `find`/`grep` fallback behavior unchanged.

## Impact

Any Windows user with ripgrep on PATH gets silently-empty `search_files`/`search` results for absolute paths. Since skills commonly pass absolute paths (e.g. an Obsidian vault location), the agent wastes turns retrying identical searches, and the tool-loop guard (`idempotent_no_progress_warning`) fires. A secondary issue worth considering separately: `rg` IO errors in `_search_files_rg` are discarded by `2>/dev/null`, so genuine failures (bad path, permissions) are indistinguishable from "no matches" — surfacing exit-code-2 diagnostics the way `_search_with_rg` does would have made this bug visible immediately.

## Summary

When `model.api_mode = codex_responses` (the default for `claude-opus-4.8`, `claude-opus-4.8-fast`, and the `gpt-5.x` family), requests to Copilot arrive at GitHub without the `Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat` header. GitHub then attributes the request to integrator `copilot-language-server`, whose model whitelist is much smaller than `vscode-chat`'s, and returns:

```
HTTP 400: The requested model is not available for integrator "copilot-language-server".
Available models: [gpt-4.1 claude-opus-4.7 gpt-5.4-mini gpt-5.5 gpt-5.6-luna gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-terra gpt-5-mini gpt-3.5-turbo gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 gpt-4o-mini
gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 copilot-preview-4o-mini-a1cfd608 gpt-4]
```

Note `claude-opus-4.7` is on the language-server whitelist and `claude-opus-4.8*` is not — which is why 4.7 keeps working and 4.8 fails on the same Copilot seat.

## Reproduction

Copilot seat (Business/Pro+) that the `/models` endpoint confirms has access to `claude-opus-4.8-fast`:

```bash
hermes config set model.provider copilot
hermes config set model.default claude-opus-4.8-fast
hermes config set model.api_mode codex_responses   # default for this model
hermes -z "hi"
# -> HTTP 400 integrator "copilot-language-server"
```

Verify the seat is fine by hitting the same model with the correct header directly:

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <copilot-jwt>" \
     -H "Editor-Version: vscode/1.104.1" \
     -H "Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4.8-fast","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":10}' \
     https://api.githubcopilot.com/chat/completions
# -> HTTP 200
```

Workaround that confirms the diagnosis:

```bash
hermes config set model.api_mode chat_completions
# opus-4.8 now works on the same account
```

## Root cause (suspected)

`run_agent.py:_apply_client_headers_for_base_url` (around line 4437) attaches `copilot_default_headers()` (which includes `Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat`) when the base URL host matches `githubcopilot.com`. That path fires for the OpenAI-SDK-based `chat_completions` client.

For `codex_responses` and the ACP/`/responses` code path (`agent/copilot_acp_client.py`, `hermes_cli/models.py` responses-mode helpers), the header set does not appear to be applied in the same way — the request reaches GitHub without `Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat`, so upstream falls back to integrator attribution `copilot-language-server`. The existing regression test `tests/run_agent/test_provider_attribution_headers.py::test_copilot_enterprise_base_url_applies_copilot_default_headers` covers only the `chat_completions` path.

## Suggested fix

Ensure every outbound Copilot request path applies the full `copilot_default_headers()` (Editor-Version, User-Agent, Copilot-Integration-Id, Openai-Intent, x-initiator) regardless of `api_mode`, including:
- `codex_responses` / `/responses` client construction
- `copilot_acp_client.CopilotACPClient` HTTP path (if it reaches `api.githubcopilot.com` directly)
- Any auxiliary/side-task clients bound to a Copilot base URL

Extend `test_provider_attribution_headers.py` with a `codex_responses` case that asserts `Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat` is on the outbound request.

## Impact

Silent model-availability degradation: users on a Copilot seat that legitimately has Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.6 / gpt-5.x-full access see them as unavailable, and the natural workaround ("pin to opus-4.7") hides the underlying header bug. Also billing-relevant: `copilot-language-server` and `vscode-chat` may bill under different Copilot quota rules on Enterprise.

## Environment

- hermes-agent HEAD: `4281151ae` (`test(gateway): cover effective context budget`)
- Provider: `copilot`
- Failing models: `claude-opus-4.8`, `claude-opus-4.8-fast` (any Copilot model not on the `copilot-language-server` whitelist)
- Working models on same account: `claude-opus-4.7`, `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-4.1`

items.body:
### Summary

`session/set_model` (ACP) fails with a generic `RequestError: Internal error` when pinning `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b` on the **nous** provider — even though the model is live on the Nous inference API (`GET /v1/models` lists it, and a CLI one-shot `hermes -z "..." -m nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b --provider nous` works fine).

### Root cause (traced in v0.16.0)

`acp_adapter/server.py::set_session_model` → `_resolve_model_selection` → `detect_provider_for_model(model, "nous")`:

1. The **static nous catalog** in `hermes_cli/models.py` contains `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` but **not** `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b` (the live Nous `/v1/models` has both).
2. Because the model is missing from the current provider's static list, detection falls through to the other static catalogs and matches the **`nvidia`** (NIM / integrate.api.nvidia.com) catalog, silently switching the provider:
   `detect_provider_for_model("nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b", "nous") -> ("nvidia", "nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b")`
3. `_make_agent` then builds an agent for the `nvidia` provider. Without an NVIDIA NIM API key this raises, and the ACP layer surfaces only `RequestError: Internal error` — every `session/new` from an ACP client that pins this model fails, and clients silently fall back to resuming old sessions (which keep their previously stored model).

### Repro

1. Nous OAuth login, no NVIDIA NIM key configured.
2. ACP: `initialize` → `session/new` → `session/set_model {"modelId": "nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b"}` → `Internal error`.
3. Control: same call with `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` (present in the static nous list) works.

### Suggested fix

- Add `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b` to the static nous catalog (verified locally: with this one-line addition, detection returns `None`, the provider stays `nous`, and `set_model` + turns work), and/or
- prefer the current provider's **live** `/v1/models` catalog over cross-provider static matches before rerouting, and
- surface the real exception instead of the generic `Internal error` (a provider switch to a keyless provider is very hard to diagnose from the ACP client side).

Environment: hermes-agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5), Windows 11, ACP stdio client.

items.title: Live messaging session killed by TUI/dashboard WS-orphan reaper; recovery then mints empty sessions (history=0) instead of reopening

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

A **live Telegram DM gateway session** can be permanently knocked into a "zombie" state by the **TUI/dashboard WebSocket orphan reaper**. When a dashboard/TUI browser client that is merely *viewing* a session disconnects, the reaper writes `ended_at`/`end_reason='ws_orphan_reap'` on the **shared `sessions` row** — the same row that is the live routing target of a messaging platform. The session keeps receiving messages, but from then on every inbound message is answered with **`history=0`** (empty context), because the recovery path does not treat `ws_orphan_reap` as recoverable and mints a fresh empty session each time. All transcript rows remain on disk (`active=1`); only the context loader ignores them.

Net user-visible effect: the bot "forgets everything" mid-conversation, context appears stuck at a few %, the session id silently changes on every message, and the DB grows with replies that are written back under the dead session id.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.18.x (observed on a git checkout at HEAD `f3af7930c`, 2026-07-06)
- Linux, Docker container; dashboard reachable over the docker bridge (`172.17.0.1`)
- Platform: Telegram DM (single long-lived working session)

## Root cause (two independent layers)

### Layer A — the reaper ends a session that is a live routing target
`tui_gateway/server.py`:
- `_ws_session_is_orphaned()` (~L660-671) returns True when a session has no live WS transport and is not mid-turn. It inspects **only** the TUI/dashboard WS transport.
- `_schedule_ws_orphan_reap()` / `_reap()` (~L674-701) then, after `_WS_ORPHAN_REAP_GRACE_S` (default **20s**, L159-165), calls `_close_session_by_id(sid, end_reason="ws_orphan_reap")`, which finalizes the **shared `sessions` row** in `state.db`.

Nothing checks whether that `session_id` is currently the **gateway routing target for a messaging platform** (e.g. a Telegram DM). So closing a dashboard tab that was viewing the session ends the live messaging session.

Observed log (UTC):
```
2026-07-10 18:20:26 tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=172.17.0.1:50027 reason=client_disconnect(code=1006) ... reaped_sessions=1
```
state.db row finalized 20s later, at `2026-07-10 18:20:46`, `end_reason=ws_orphan_reap`. Exact grace-window match.

### Layer B — recovery filter does not whitelist `ws_orphan_reap`
`hermes_state.py::find_latest_gateway_session_for_peer()` (~L1958-2020), both WHERE clauses:
```sql
AND (ended_at IS NULL OR end_reason = 'agent_close')
```
`ws_orphan_reap` is not in the allowlist, so `_recover_session_from_db()` (`gateway/session.py` L1295-1331) returns None. `get_or_create_session()` then falls through to **create a brand-new empty session** (L1764+) for the routing key. Meanwhile the `#54878` live-gateway stale-routing guard (`gateway/session.py` L1683-1691) fires on every inbound message because the DB row is `ended`, dropping the routing entry and re-minting again.

Evidence: on the affected routing key, **5 freshly-minted session rows each with 0 messages** were created across one afternoon, while the real session row holds 369+ messages (all `active=1`) and `history=` in the turn logs collapsed `157 → 0` and never recovered.

Note: the reopen machinery already exists and works — `_recover_session_from_db` calls `reopen_session(recovered["id"])` and reloads the transcript. It simply is never reached for `ws_orphan_reap` rows.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Run the gateway serving a Telegram (or any messaging platform) DM as a long-lived session.
2. Open the dashboard/TUI in a browser and view that session (this attaches a WS transport to the session id).
3. Close the dashboard tab / let the WS disconnect (no reconnect within the 20s grace).
4. The reaper finalizes the session row with `end_reason='ws_orphan_reap'`.
5. Send another Telegram message to the same DM.
6. **Observed:** the reply is generated with `history=0`; a new empty session id is minted; the transcript is ignored. **Expected:** the existing session continues with full history — a dashboard viewer disconnecting must not end a live messaging session.

## Suggested fix
- **Layer B (minimal, self-healing):** add `ws_orphan_reap` to the recovery allowlist in `find_latest_gateway_session_for_peer` (both WHERE clauses): `end_reason IN ('agent_close', 'ws_orphan_reap')`. This makes any wrongly-reaped session reopen with its transcript intact on the next inbound message.
- **Layer A (prevention):** `_ws_session_is_orphaned()` (or the `_reap` guard) must not reap a session that is the current gateway routing target for a messaging platform. A dashboard/TUI viewer detaching should never finalize a live cross-platform session row.

Both are small and independent; Layer B alone already neutralizes the user-visible data loss, Layer A prevents the false finalize in the first place.

## Impact
High for anyone running the dashboard against a live messaging gateway: a routine "close the dashboard tab" silently lobotomizes an active conversation, with no error surfaced to the user. Data is not lost on disk but is invisible to the model until the row's `ended` flag is manually cleared.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop composer not ready on new session — first Enter fails, message stays in input, needs second send

items.body:
**Description**
In Hermes Desktop (Windows 10, build from 2026-07-12, version files 0.18.2), when opening a **new chat** (or switching sessions) and sending the first message:
1. The message text from the **previous** chat remains visible in the composer input field.
2. Pressing **Enter the first time** does nothing — the message stays in the input and is not sent.
3. Pressing **Enter a second time** sends the message and clears the input; after that the chat works normally.

Reproduces 100% of the time on the first message of every new session.

**Root cause (from logs + bundle analysis)**
`desktop.log` contains:
```
[hermes] [renderer console] Uncaught Error: Composer is not available
(file:///.../win-unpacked/resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-BK_BHFlU.js:4103)
```
In the renderer bundle, the composer wrapper classes (`rCi`/`iCi` thread-composer, `aCi` edit-composer) throw `Composer is not available` when `_composerApi.getState()` returns `null`. The `send()`/`setText()`/`reset()` methods all guard with `if(!t)throw Error("Composer is not available")`. On a fresh session the composer API state is `null` at the moment of the first Enter, so the send is dropped; by the second Enter the composer has mounted and `getState()` is non-null, so it works. This is a session-switch / mount-timing race in the Desktop UI layer (similar class to issue #46563).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open Hermes Desktop.
2. Start a new chat (or switch to a different session).
3. Type a message and press Enter once.
4. Observe: message is not sent, text remains in input.
5. Press Enter again -> message sends and input clears.

**Expected**
First Enter sends the message and clears the input; the input should not retain text from a previous session when a new session is opened.

**Environment**
- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes: 0.18.2 (version files consistent)
- Desktop build: win-unpacked, `resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-BK_BHFlU.js`
- Already tried: clearing `%APPDATA%\Hermes\Local Storage\leveldb` (composer-drafts cache) — did NOT fix it, confirming it is a runtime mount-timing bug, not stale cache.

**Possible fix direction**
Make the composer wrapper resilient to `null` state: queue `send()`/`setText()` and flush once `_composerApi.getState()` becomes available, instead of throwing `Composer is not available`.

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the WhatsApp gateway reconnect loop opens visible console windows whenever the bridge is unhealthy or awaiting re-pairing. The windows are created by short-lived console subprocesses launched without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`.

In a 30-minute capture, 15 visible Windows Terminal/OpenConsole windows appeared: three per reconnect cycle across five cycles, with each cycle roughly 5 minutes 34 seconds apart.

## Environment

- Windows 11
- Hermes Agent 0.18.2
- Reproduced on commit `8e3f9537db21b49ebe796f7b5a6ff489028fe1fb`
- Confirmed still present on current `main` candidate `7b5ba2054721dde998ed47fd4a0f031955278e99`
- WhatsApp mode: `self-chat`
- Trigger condition: bridge connection times out / account requires re-pairing

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the WhatsApp platform on Windows.
2. Use a session that cannot connect and requires re-pairing, or otherwise force the bridge to time out.
3. Start the Hermes gateway.
4. Leave the reconnect watcher running.

## Actual behavior

Each reconnect cycle produces visible terminal flashes:

1. Two short flashes around the Node requirement probes.
2. One longer flash when the timed-out bridge is terminated.

The gateway log repeats:

```text
Reconnecting whatsapp (attempt N)...
Reconnect whatsapp error: whatsapp connect timed out after 30s, next retry in 300s
```

Process/window tracing aligned the flashes with:

- `node.exe --version`
- `node.exe .../whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js`
- `taskkill /PID ... /T` after the 30-second timeout

The Node probe windows were typically visible for only a few milliseconds; the timeout cleanup window was visible for roughly 0.5–0.6 seconds.

## Expected behavior

All WhatsApp gateway background subprocesses should run without creating or activating a visible console window.

## Root cause

In `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`, these Windows subprocess calls do not pass the existing `windows_hide_flags()` compatibility helper:

- `_terminate_bridge_process()`: `taskkill`
- `check_whatsapp_requirements()`: `node --version`
- WhatsApp dependency repair: `npm install --silent`

The long-running bridge `Popen` already uses `windows_detach_popen_kwargs()`, and the port-cleanup `netstat` / `taskkill` path already uses `windows_hide_flags()`.

## Suggested fix

Import `windows_hide_flags` alongside `windows_detach_popen_kwargs` and pass:

```python
creationflags=windows_hide_flags()
```

to the three `subprocess.run()` calls above. The helper returns `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on Windows and `0` elsewhere.

## Validation

A local patch was tested with:

- 16 passing Windows subprocess regression tests
- Focused async tests for the npm-install and bridge-taskkill paths
- End-to-end process/window monitoring across multiple real reconnect attempts

Before the patch: 15 visible terminal windows over five reconnect cycles.

After the patch and gateway restart: 0 visible windows while the monitor recorded 908 process-start events, including repeated real `bridge.js` starts and `taskkill.exe` timeout cleanup.

## Related

The same Windows console-flash class is being addressed for another platform in #54565.

items.title: [Bug]: `LocalEnvironment._update_cwd()` reads back a temp file it just wrote — redundant file I/O on every `terminal()` call

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

Every `terminal()` call does a redundant file read. The shell bootstrap writes the current working directory to a temp file via shell redirection, then `_update_cwd()` immediately opens and reads that same file back in Python — even though the same __HERMES_CWD_<session>__ marker is already present in the result's stdout (emitted on base.py:424) and can be parsed in-process by _extract_cwd_from_output() — the base method every remote backend already relies on. The local override bypasses that marker and reads the temp file instead of `[base.py](https://base.py/)`. The temp file read at line 1162 of `[local.py](https://local.py/)` duplicates work that was already done.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run any terminal command (e.g. `ls`, `pwd`, `git status`)
2. Watch the temp file:

```bash
watch -n 0.5 'cat [/tmp](tg://bot_command?command=tmp)[/hermes](tg://bot_command?command=hermes)-cwd-*.txt 2>/dev/null'
```

Every command rewrites and re-reads this file. With ~2-3 terminal calls/second during active use, that's ~12,000 file I/O operations per hour.

Alternatively, run with `strace`:

```bash
strace -e trace=openat -p $(pgrep -f "hermes-agent") 2>&1 | grep hermes-cwd
```

### Expected Behavior

The working directory should be tracked entirely from the stdout marker (which was designed for this purpose and already parsed by `_extract_cwd_from_output()` in `[base.py](https://base.py/)`). No redundant temp file read should occur.

### Actual Behavior

Every terminal command triggers:
1. Shell writes `pwd -P > [/tmp](tg://bot_command?command=tmp)[/hermes](tg://bot_command?command=hermes)-cwd-<session>.txt` (already unnecessary for local execution since the marker is in stdout)
2. Python immediately reads it back: `open(self._cwd_file).read().strip()`
3. The local backend maintains cwd through a second, divergent mechanism (temp file) instead of the marker parser used by all other backends. Beyond the redundant read, this means local and remote backends can disagree on cwd in edge cases, and the temp-file path must stay in sync with the marker logic forever.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream 4281151a
Install directory: /home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent
Install method: git
Python: 3.11.2
```

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)

### Python Version

Python 3.11.2

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Two parallel mechanisms exist for discovering the working directory after a terminal command:

Mechanism A — stdout marker (correct): Line 424 of base.py emits printf '\n__HERMES_CWD_<id>__%s__HERMES_CWD_<id>__\n' "$(pwd -P)" after every command. Base class method _extract_cwd_from_output(result) parses this marker from stdout and updates self.cwd. This works for all backends — local, Docker, SSH, Modal.

Mechanism B — temp file (redundant): Line 423 of base.py writes pwd -P > /tmp/hermes-cwd-<id>.txt. Then local.py's _update_cwd() override (line 1162) ignores the already-parsed stdout marker and reads this file back:

```
# local.py line 1162
with open(self._cwd_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    cwd_path = f.read().strip()
```
This is a case of two mechanisms doing the same job. The file was originally added as a fallback for remote backends where stdout parsing can be unreliable, but local.py overrides the base class method to always use the file instead of delegating to the already-working marker parser.

git blame base.py:423 / local.py:1162

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Option 1:
3-line change in local.py:

Replace the file read with a delegation to the base class's marker parser:

```
def _update_cwd(self, result: dict):
    # cwd is already in the stdout marker — no temp file read needed.
    self._extract_cwd_from_output(result)
```
That's it. The shell can keep writing the temp file (it doesn't hurt remote backends that actually need it); the local backend just stops reading it back.

Option 2:
For a cleaner fix: Gate the shell redirection behind a not-local check (base.py line 423), so local execution doesn't write the file at all:
```
f"printf '\\n%s%%s%s\\n' \"${{self._cwd_marker}}\" \"$(pwd -P)\"\\n"  # always emit marker
if not self._IS_LOCAL:
    f"pwd -P > {_quoted_cwd_file} 2>/dev/null || true\\n"  # only for remote backends
```
Preferred: gate the redirection behind not self._IS_LOCAL (base.py:423) so local execution never creates /tmp/hermes-cwd-<id>.txt. This also removes a predictable-path temp file in a shared directory (minor local-integrity/info-disclosure surface), making it the safer choice, not just the cleaner one.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

# Bug: 同一会话ID的侧边栏在不同窗口显示条目数不一致，且缺失条目永不补回

## 发现

同一 Hermes 会话（相同 session_id），在两个不同窗口中打开的侧边栏（conversation history sidebar）显示的条目数不同——一个显示 12 条，另一个显示 11 条，缺失了中间的一条消息。

## 复现步骤

1. 在窗口 A 中与 Hermes 进行一系列对话（约 12 轮问答）
2. 在窗口 A 中继续问问题（第 12 条）
3. 打开该会话的窗口 B（新窗口，加载同一 session_id）
4. 窗口 B 的侧边栏只显示了 11 条条目，第 12 条（在窗口 A 中已存在）未显示
5. 继续在窗口 B 中问新问题
6. 新问题的条目正常出现在侧边栏，但缺失的第 12 条从未被补回

## 预期行为

- 同一 session_id 的所有窗口应显示相同的侧边栏条目
- 如果侧边栏在窗口打开时做了数据快照，后续的增量更新应能够检测并填补快照与数据库当前状态之间的缺口（gap-fill）

## 实际行为

- 窗口 B 的侧边栏初始化时读到了 11 条（缺失第 12 条）
- 后续的增量更新只追加了新消息（第 13、14 条...），但从未回溯填充第 12 条
- 缺失的条目**永久丢失**，即使窗口 B 继续使用

## 推测根因

侧边栏的加载逻辑疑似是：
1. 窗口打开时，从 `state.db`（SQLite session store）做一次全量索引查询，获取当前所有消息条目
2. 之后用户继续对话时，只做**增量追加**（查询最新消息ID之后的新消息）
3. 没有**一致性校验步骤**来检测初始化时的查询结果与数据库实际记录之间的差异

如果窗口 B 打开的时刻，数据库写入（第 12 条消息的持久化）与侧边栏查询之间存在微小的时序差，第 12 条可能被遗漏。更关键的是，增量更新逻辑没有补齐这个缺口。

## 环境

- Hermes 版本：（请用户补充）
- 运行界面：Electron 桌面端（Desktop GUI）
- 操作系统：Windows 10

## 附加说明

- 该问题不是简单的"时序竞态"——用户在窗口 A 中完成第 12 次问答后等待了数分钟才打开窗口 B，第 12 条消息的持久化已确信完成
- 即使窗口 B 继续进行了多次对话，缺失的条目也从未出现

items.title: bug(telegram): post-reconnect probe routes auth errors into reconnect ladder and bypasses the recovery dedup guard (gap left by #62098)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

#62098 fixed PTB transport-error classification for the polling heartbeat loop and the pending-update probe, but the **third** probe in the same family was left out: `_verify_polling_after_reconnect()` (the one-shot probe scheduled 60s after a successful reconnect) still has both of the pre-#62098 problems, plus a concurrency gap:

1. **No classification.** Its `except Exception` routes *every* `get_me()` failure into `_handle_polling_network_error()` — including `InvalidToken` / `Forbidden` / `BadRequest`, which `_looks_like_network_error()` (adapter.py:1185) deliberately excludes everywhere else since #62098.

2. **Dedup-guard bypass.** It `await`s `_handle_polling_network_error()` directly (two call sites) instead of registering the recovery as `_polling_error_task`. While that inline recovery is mid-flight (stop → drain → start_polling, with 5–60s backoff), the 90s heartbeat loop's guard sees `_polling_error_task.done() == True` and can schedule a **second concurrent recovery**. Two overlapping stop/drain/start_polling sequences produce dueling getUpdates sessions — the self-inflicted 409 Conflict loop that `_disarm_ptb_retry_loop()`'s own docstring warns about.

3. (Minor) The probe-failure `logger.warning` logs the error unredacted; PTB transport error text can embed the `api.telegram.org/bot<token>/...` request URL. Sibling sites use `_redact_telegram_error_text()`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Trigger a reconnect (any transient network error) that succeeds — `_handle_polling_network_error` schedules `_verify_polling_after_reconnect` via `asyncio.ensure_future` (adapter.py:2153).
2. Revoke the bot token (or force `get_me()` to raise `InvalidToken`) before the 60s probe fires.
3. Observe: the probe feeds `InvalidToken` into the network-reconnect ladder — up to 10 exponential-backoff stop/drain/start cycles (~5+ minutes) before going fatal as `telegram_network_error`, masking the real auth failure.

For the race: make the post-reconnect probe's `get_me()` hang/fail while the heartbeat loop's next tick also fails — the heartbeat schedules a second `_handle_polling_network_error` because `_polling_error_task` is not the in-flight recovery.

### Expected Behavior

- Non-connectivity probe failures (auth/validation) should not enter the reconnect ladder — same policy as the heartbeat loop and pending-update probe after #62098.
- All recovery entry points should route through `_schedule_polling_recovery()` so the in-flight guard, fatal-error guard, and task bookkeeping apply uniformly.

### Actual Behavior

`InvalidToken` from the post-reconnect probe triggers network-reconnect churn; concurrent recoveries are possible via the dedup-guard bypass.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram)

### Environment

Current `main` (verified at 7b5ba2054).

I have a fix ready and will open a PR shortly.

items.title: Discord "Always" approval resolves the command but never persists to command_allowlist (group-session path)

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

In a Discord **group session** (server channel, not DM), pressing the **"Always"** button on a command-approval prompt resolves the pending command — it runs — but the pattern is **never persisted to `command_allowlist`**. The next occurrence of the same command prompts again, forever.

## Environment

- hermes-agent **v0.18.2**
- Gateway running as a LaunchAgent on macOS (arm64), Discord adapter
- Session type: Discord **server channel** ("group session"); user is allowlist-gated, `allowed_channels='*'`
- Approval prompt delivered as Discord buttons (Approve once / Always / Deny)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the gateway with the Discord adapter and let the agent attempt a shell command that is not on `command_allowlist` (e.g. a custom wrapper script).
2. In a **server channel** session, wait for the approval prompt and press **Always**.
3. Observe the command executes (pending approval is resolved correctly).
4. Ask the agent to run the same command again.

## Expected

Per the CLI semantics ("always" → `approve_session` + `approve_permanent` + `save_permanent_allowlist`), the pattern key should be appended to the permanent allowlist, and step 4 should run without a prompt.

## Actual

Step 4 prompts again. The permanent allowlist file is unchanged after step 2 (verified by diffing it before/after). Only the in-flight command was approved — "Always" behaved exactly like "Approve once".

## Notes / where we looked

- The gateway persistence branch in `tools/approval.py` (the `_await_gateway_decision` caller) looks correct at HEAD: on `choice == "always"` it calls `approve_session` + `approve_permanent` + `save_permanent_allowlist` — but the persistence loop iterates the `warnings` list (`for key, _, is_tirith in warnings:`), so if that list is empty on this path, an approved "always" silently persists nothing.
- We could not rule out that the Discord button in group sessions resolves with a different choice value (e.g. downgraded to session scope the way a tirith warning does) — DM sessions were not affected the same way in our testing.

## Workaround

Manually adding glob patterns to `command_allowlist` in config works and is what we're running with, but it bypasses the whole point of the "Always" button.

Happy to provide gateway logs for a repro run if useful.

items.title: [Bug]: Self-hosted OIDC JWKS fetch fails behind Cloudflare due to PyJWKClient default headers

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
### Bug Description

Dashboard self-hosted OIDC can fail after a successful IdP authorization when the configured issuer's JWKS endpoint is behind Cloudflare or a similar WAF.

The browser completes the OIDC flow, but Hermes then fails while retrieving the public signing key needed to verify the ID token and reports:

```text
Auth provider 'self-hosted' unreachable
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.18.2` (`2026.7.7.2`)
- Python `3.11`
- PyJWT `2.13.0`
- Dashboard self-hosted OIDC provider
- Public HTTPS issuer/JWKS endpoint behind Cloudflare

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a self-hosted OIDC issuer whose discovery document advertises a public HTTPS `jwks_uri`.
2. Put that JWKS route behind a Cloudflare/WAF policy that permits normal browser requests but rejects Python's default `urllib` fingerprint.
3. Confirm:
   - OIDC discovery succeeds.
   - A browser-compatible request to the exact JWKS URI returns `HTTP 200`.
   - Python `urllib` to that same URI returns `HTTP 403` (Cloudflare error `1010` in this case).
4. Start dashboard login and complete authentication at the IdP.

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should be able to retrieve a valid public JWKS response from common CDN/WAF-fronted OIDC issuers without requiring a local source patch, while retaining normal TLS and JWT signature verification.

### Actual Behavior

The authorization-code exchange completes, but Hermes cannot retrieve the signing key for ID-token verification.

The dashboard fails closed with a self-hosted provider-unreachable error.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
N/A
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`SelfHostedOIDCProvider._get_jwks_client()` constructs `jwt.PyJWKClient` without request headers.

PyJWT `2.13.0` supports a `headers=` parameter, but Hermes currently leaves it unset, so the JWKS request uses Python `urllib`'s default fingerprint. Some Cloudflare policies reject that request even though the endpoint is otherwise healthy.

## Proposed fix

Pass a small, explicit API-client header set to `PyJWKClient`:

```python
_JWKS_REQUEST_HEADERS = {
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Hermes Dashboard OIDC)",
    "Accept": "application/json",
}

PyJWKClient(
    disco["jwks_uri"],
    cache_keys=True,
    lifespan=_JWKS_CACHE_SECONDS,
    headers=dict(_JWKS_REQUEST_HEADERS),
)
```

This changes only the HTTP headers used for the public JWKS GET request. It does not disable or relax:

- TLS validation
- JWT signature validation
- issuer validation
- audience validation
- PKCE
- session-cookie security
- JWKS caching/key-rotation behaviour

## Validation

With the header override:

- focused regression test passes;
- the real `get_signing_keys()` call retrieves the IdP signing key;
- dashboard OIDC login completes successfully;
- authenticated WebSocket ticket minting succeeds.

I searched existing Hermes issues for `PyJWKClient`, `JWKS lookup failed`, and `JWKS 403`; I did not find an existing report for this client-header compatibility failure.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

### Bug Description

### Summary

Both `provider: custom` and `provider: azure-foundry` (with `api_mode: chat_completions`) send the API key via `Authorization: Bearer <key>` for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, with no configuration option to override the header name. This breaks any gateway that requires a differently-named header — specifically, an Azure API Management (APIM) instance fronting an Azure OpenAI/Foundry deployment, which requires the header literally named `api-key` (Azure OpenAI's native convention). Every request fails with HTTP 401, even though the same key and endpoint work correctly via a raw `curl` request using the `api-key` header.

This is the mirror image of #26970 (Azure Foundry sending `x-api-key` when Bearer was needed, for `anthropic_messages` transport) — but on the OpenAI-style `chat_completions` transport, and triggered by an APIM domain (`*.azure-api.net`) rather than a direct Foundry domain (`*.openai.azure.com`).

### Environment

- Hermes Agent: `v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)`
- Profile: custom named profile (not default)
- Endpoint: university-provisioned Azure APIM gateway fronting an Azure OpenAI deployment
- Base URL: `https://apim-n1ai-usw2-89fbd882c.azure-api.net/openai/v1`
- Model: `gpt-5.4`
- Verified working header via direct `curl`: `api-key: <key>`



### Steps to Reproduce


### Reproduction

**Setup** — `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/config.yaml`:
```yaml
model:
  provider: azure-foundry
  base_url: https://apim-n1ai-usw2-89fbd882c.azure-api.net/openai/v1
  api_mode: chat_completions
  default: gpt-5.4
  api_key: <redacted>
```

**Step 1** — confirm the key and endpoint work correctly outside Hermes:
```bash
curl -i -H "api-key: <redacted>" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  https://apim-n1ai-usw2-89fbd882c.azure-api.net/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_completion_tokens":10}'
```
Result: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, valid completion returned.

**Step 2** — run the same request through Hermes:
```bash
hermes -p <profile> chat -q "hello"
```

Result:
⚠️  API call failed (attempt 1/3): AuthenticationError [HTTP 401]
🔌 Provider: azure-foundry  Model: gpt-5.4
🌐 Endpoint: https://apim-n1ai-usw2-89fbd882c.azure-api.net/openai/v1
📝 Error: HTTP 401: Access denied due to missing subscription key. Make sure to include subscription key when making requests to an API.

That error text is APIM's own native rejection for "no recognized auth header present" — confirming Hermes is not sending `api-key` for this transport/provider combination.

**Step 3** — same result under `provider: custom` (generic OpenAI-compatible path) instead of `azure-foundry`; both send `Authorization: Bearer` regardless.

### Expected Behavior

For `chat_completions`-mode custom/Azure-Foundry providers, Hermes should either:
- Detect Azure OpenAI-style endpoints and send the `api-key` header the way Azure's own SDK/portal samples do (mirroring the `_requires_bearer_auth` domain-sniffing already used for the `anthropic_messages` side in #26970/#28084), broadened to also cover APIM-fronted domains (`*.azure-api.net`) rather than only `*.openai.azure.com`; or
- Expose an explicit config field (e.g. `auth_header_name:`) so users can specify the exact header name for any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, independent of domain-sniffing.

The second option would also generalize to other institutional API gateways with idiosyncratic header requirements, not just Azure's.

### Actual Behavior

Every request is sent with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` regardless of `provider` (`custom` or `azure-foundry`) or the target domain, with no way to override this from `config.yaml`. Requests to `*.azure-api.net`-fronted Azure OpenAI deployments fail 100% of the time with HTTP 401.

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/eb3qB
agent.log    https://paste.rs/TEU6Y
gateway.log  https://paste.rs/99eN5
gui.log      https://paste.rs/oqpP3
desktop.log  https://dpaste.com/E7EWUJQNK
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

- Extend the domain-sniffing logic used for the Anthropic-transport fix in #28084 to also apply to the OpenAI-wire (`chat_completions`) client construction, and broaden the domain match beyond `*.openai.azure.com` to include APIM-fronted domains.
- Alternatively/additionally, add a generic `auth_header_name` (or similar) field to the `model:` / `custom_providers:` schema, so any custom endpoint's header name is user-configurable without relying on domain heuristics at all.

items.body:
## Summary

After upgrading to Hermes Agent v0.18.2, the Telegram gateway adapter hangs indefinitely at the first connection attempt (`Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…`) and never recovers. The 30-second `asyncio.wait_for` timeout around `Application.initialize()` does not fire, so no retry is attempted. This matches the behavior described in #59202, but reproduces here even after manual restarts and is not limited to early container boot.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream 7b5ba205
- Python 3.11.15 (venv)
- Install method: git
- Host: LightOS container (lazy-cat / 懒猫微服) inside a privileged Docker container running TUN-mode proxy on the host.
- Network: default route via `100.64.0.1`, DNS `100.64.0.1`.

## Symptom

`hermes gateway status` reports the service as running, but logs are stuck at:

```
WARNING hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS…
WARNING hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…
```

No further output is produced, even after waiting well past the configured 30-second init timeout. The process does not crash; systemd sees it as healthy.

## Network sanity checks (from the same container)

```
$ getent hosts api.telegram.org
2001::c73b:9627 api.telegram.org

$ curl -sS --max-time 10 https://www.google.com/
HTTP 200 1.46s

$ curl -sS --max-time 10 https://api.telegram.org/botFAKE/getMe
HTTP 404 1.36s

$ curl -sS --resolve api.telegram.org:443:149.154.167.220 --max-time 10 https://api.telegram.org/botFAKE/getMe
HTTP 404 1.09s

$ /home/kevin/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -c "
import asyncio, httpx
async def t():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10) as c:
        r = await c.get('https://api.telegram.org/botFAKE/getMe')
        print(r.status_code)
asyncio.run(t())
"
404
```

The 404 responses are expected (invalid token), but they prove that TCP/TLS connectivity to `api.telegram.org` is fully functional from the same venv and the same network namespace.

## Why this is likely not a simple connectivity problem

1. Direct `httpx` and `curl` calls reach Telegram immediately.
2. The gateway logs never show the `Connect attempt 1/8 timed out after 30s — retrying in Xs` message, suggesting the event loop is blocked before `asyncio.wait_for` can fire its timeout.
3. The problem started immediately after `hermes update` and persists across `systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway.service`.

## Related

- #59202 — same logger (`hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter`) and same "first attempt hang" symptom. In that report the issue was transient and resolved by a manual restart; here it persists across restarts.
- #59614 — Telegram polling reconnect hangs indefinitely.

## Request

Please investigate whether `Application.initialize()` in `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` can perform a blocking DNS/socket call that prevents the `asyncio.wait_for` timeout from firing, and consider moving the initial connectivity probe off the main event loop (e.g., `asyncio.to_thread`) or adding a lower-level socket connect timeout.

items.title: MoA: add periodic advisor refresh cadence for tool-heavy turns

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

MoA's advisor fan-out is valuable on difficult tasks, but its present cadence creates a multiplicative latency failure in tool-heavy turns.

With `fanout: per_iteration`, Hermes re-runs every reference model after every tool result before the aggregator can decide the next action. A task that should be a short smoke test can therefore become multiple sequential rounds of:

1. wait for all advisors;
2. wait for the acting aggregator;
3. execute one tool operation;
4. repeat.

A user running two references reported a roughly 4m45s smoke test for this reason. That is an anecdote rather than a benchmark, but the mechanism is deterministic: each additional tool-loop state adds at least one more slowest-advisor round trip.

`reference_max_tokens` reduces generation time, but does not remove the repeated network/model latency or the repeated advisor input processing. `user_turn` avoids the repetition, but then the aggregator never gets a fresh independent view after a long tool loop changes the task state materially.

## Request

Add a first-class middle cadence between the current modes:

- references run once at the beginning of every user turn;
- during the same tool loop, they refresh only after a configurable number of meaningful tool-state advances;
- the acting aggregator reuses the most recent reference guidance between refreshes.

This should be a product-level configuration decision, not merely a local workaround. The goal is to preserve MoA's independent criticism at meaningful checkpoints without turning routine tool use into a committee meeting after every command.

## Design questions worth resolving upstream

I am deliberately not submitting a PR here: the right API and state semantics should be chosen by maintainers who know the agent loop and model-selection surfaces better than I do.

1. **What counts as one refresh unit?**
   Prefer a completed *tool-call batch/state advance* rather than an individual tool-result message. A single aggregator action can emit parallel calls; counting every individual result could unexpectedly trigger a refresh in the middle of one logical action.

2. **What should trigger a refresh?**
   A new user turn must always get initial advice. Within a turn, refresh after `N` completed batches that changed available evidence. Retried transport failures or duplicate/no-progress results may not deserve an expensive new advisory pass.

3. **How should the configuration read?**
   The existing `fanout` enum could gain a periodic option plus a positive interval, or the system could use a clearer general cadence abstraction. Existing `per_iteration` and `user_turn` behavior must remain unchanged by default.

4. **Prompt-cache invariant.**
   Fresh reference guidance must remain tail context for the acting aggregator, never mutate the stable system/history prefix. Reuse should not cause duplicated reference blocks or re-charge advisor accounting on cache hits.

5. **UX/observability.**
   The MoA UI currently surfaces advisor activity. It should make clear whether guidance was freshly refreshed or reused, otherwise a long silent aggregator step can be misread as a stalled reference fan-out.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new user turn fans out to advisors exactly once before the first acting-model call.
- A tool-heavy turn with interval `N=7` does not re-run advisors after state advances 1–6, then does re-run them after the seventh completed tool batch.
- Parallel tool calls are defined and tested as one batch or explicitly documented otherwise.
- The refresh sees the full current advisory view, including recent tool outputs.
- Existing `per_iteration` and `user_turn` behavior stays backward-compatible.
- Reference usage/cost accounting is charged exactly once per actual fan-out.
- The main conversation and aggregator prompt-cache prefix stay byte-stable.
- Configuration appears coherently in CLI, Desktop, Dashboard, docs, and model-picker preset management.

## Why this matters

This is not mainly a token-cost complaint. With strong aggregators, people will reasonably want MoA for ordinary work because the outputs can be excellent. The current all-or-nothing choice forces an ugly trade: stale initial advice (`user_turn`) or several minutes of latency for mundane multi-step operations (`per_iteration`). A periodic checkpoint cadence makes MoA viable outside rare architecture/debug sessions while retaining the thing that makes it interesting: independent criticism after the world has changed.
