items.body:
## Summary

Cards created with `--goal` never exercise the Ralph-style goal loop. The dispatcher sets `HERMES_KANBAN_GOAL_MODE=1` in the worker env, but the spawned worker command (`hermes -p <profile> chat -q "work kanban task <id>"`) takes the *single-query* branch of `main()`, which never reads that env var. The goal hook is only wired in the fully-quiet `-Q/--quiet` machine-readable branch. Result: `goal_mode` is stored on the card and silently ignored; any apparent progress comes from the dispatcher's ordinary retry loop, and a worker that leaves the task open (expecting the judge to continue it) is reaped as `protocol_violation`.

## Where the wires cross (0.16.0 line numbers; same structure in 0.18.2)

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:6673-6676` (`_default_spawn`) — sets `HERMES_KANBAN_GOAL_MODE=1` and spawns `[hermes, -p, <profile>, --accept-hooks, chat, -q, <prompt>]`. The comment says *"the worker reads these and wraps its run in the Ralph-style /goal judge loop (see cli.py quiet-mode path)"* — but the spawned form never reaches that path.
- `cli.py:16010-16014` — the only reader of `HERMES_KANBAN_GOAL_MODE`, calling `_run_kanban_goal_loop_q(...)`. It lives in the `-Q/--quiet` machine-readable branch (the same block that owns the kanban EX_TEMPFAIL exit-code contract).
- `cli.py:16048-16070` — the `else` branch, explicitly documented *"Single-query mode (`hermes chat -q "…"`)"*: `cli.chat(query)` + `_print_exit_summary()`. No goal hook.

## Evidence from a live board

Worker logs of a `goal_mode` card end with the `_print_exit_summary()` block ("Resume this session with… / Duration / Messages") and never contain the `session_id:` stderr line of the quiet branch — although `_default_spawn` merges stderr into the log (`stderr=subprocess.STDOUT`, kanban_db.py:6768). Three consecutive runs of one goal card each produced exactly one turn in a fresh session, no judge verdict, no continuation; `goals.run_kanban_goal_loop` itself works when invoked directly (unit-style, mocked `cli`).

## Still present in 0.18.2 (latest)

- spawn unchanged: `kanban_db.py:7794-7796` still `["chat", "-q", prompt]`
- hook unchanged: `cli.py:16113` (quiet branch) vs single-query branch `16152-16171`

## Suggested fix (either side works)

1. Wire the `HERMES_KANBAN_GOAL_MODE` check into the single-query branch too (after `cli.chat(...)` returns the first response), or
2. Spawn goal-mode workers through the `-Q/--quiet` path the hook already lives in.

items.title: [Bug]: Provider auto-detection discards credential pools and disables failover

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

Provider auto-detection can silently discard a valid credential pool, leaving the agent without credential rotation or failover.

When `AIAgent` is constructed with `provider=None` and a recognized OpenAI Codex, xAI, or Anthropic endpoint, Hermes eventually infers the correct provider and API mode. However, credential-pool validation runs first and compares the pool with an empty provider identity, so a correctly scoped pool is rejected.

This is a regression from #63048, which correctly added provider-boundary validation but placed it before the existing URL-based provider inference.

## Steps to Reproduce

On current `main` (`7b5ba2054721`):

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from run_agent import AIAgent

pool = SimpleNamespace(provider="anthropic")
agent = AIAgent(
    provider=None,
    base_url="https://api.anthropic.com",
    api_key="test-key",
    model="test-model",
    credential_pool=pool,
    skip_context_files=True,
    skip_memory=True,
    quiet_mode=True,
)

print(agent.provider)
print(agent.api_mode)
print(agent._credential_pool is pool)
```

Observed:

```text
anthropic
anthropic_messages
False
```

## Expected Behavior

Hermes should infer `anthropic` before validating the pool. A pool scoped to Anthropic should remain attached to the agent and available for credential rotation and failover.

Pools belonging to another provider must continue to be rejected.

## Actual Behavior

Hermes infers the correct provider and API mode, but `agent._credential_pool` is `None` because the pool was validated against an empty provider identity earlier in initialization.

## Affected Component

Agent Core

## Platform

N/A; this is an agent-initialization issue shared by all surfaces that construct an agent without an explicit provider.

## Debug Report

Not applicable. This is a deterministic constructor-level regression reproduced on current `main` without user configuration, network access, or live credentials.

## Environment

- OS: Linux 6.8.0-134-generic, x86_64
- Python: 3.12.3
- Hermes commit: `7b5ba2054721`

## Root Cause Analysis

In `agent/agent_init.py`, `credential_pool_matches_provider()` is called while `agent.provider` is still empty. URL-based provider inference happens later in the API-mode selection chain.

Because scoped pools fail closed for empty provider identities, the matching pool is discarded before Hermes recognizes the endpoint.

## Proposed Fix

Resolve the explicit or URL-inferred provider before credential-pool validation, then select the API mode independently. Preserve the provider-isolation behavior from #63048 so mismatched pools still fail closed.

I have a focused fix with constructor-level regression coverage ready for submission.

### Summary

Sessions created through the web dashboard's Chat tab (`hermes dashboard --tui`) are not persisted to `state.db`, even after full conversations with hundreds of messages. The sessions exist only in the TUI gateway process's memory. When the dashboard process is restarted (e.g., via `hermes update` or systemd restart), all such sessions are lost irrecoverably.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Backend: `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --no-open --tui --skip-build` (systemd service)
- Remote desktop app connecting to the dashboard backend
- Single profile (default), `state.db` at `~/.hermes/state.db`

### Reproduction

1. Start `hermes dashboard --tui` as a persistent backend
2. Open the dashboard's Chat tab in a browser and have a full conversation (many messages, tool calls, etc.)
3. Restart the dashboard process (or run `hermes update`)
4. The session is gone — not in `state.db`, not visible in the desktop app's sidebar, not recoverable via `hermes sessions list`

### Expected behavior

Sessions from the dashboard's Chat tab should be persisted to `state.db` on first message (via `_persist_session` on `prompt.submit`), the same as CLI/TUI sessions. The `tui_gateway/server.py` code at `_maybe_persist_session_row` (line ~1662) is designed to do exactly this — but the session rows never appear in the database.

### Actual behavior

The session exists in the TUI gateway's in-memory session dict and is visible in the dashboard's own session list (which reads from the live process), but `state.db` has no record of it. Confirmed by:

- `hermes sessions list` — session not present
- Direct SQLite query (`SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id = '...'`) — no row
- Pre-update `state.db` snapshot — also not present (session was never written, not lost during update)

### Evidence

Agent log shows a full TUI conversation on the morning of July 12, 2026:

```
2026-07-12 11:48:14,652 INFO [20260712_101744_aa1323] agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=20260712_101744_aa1323 model=glm-5.2 provider=ollama-cloud platform=tui history=267 msg='where do I set reset password? When LDAP change password is set the auth failed...'
```

This session had 267 messages of history — a full, multi-hour conversation including Authentik MFA configuration, AD certificate setup, and session lifetime changes. The session ID `20260712_101744_aa1323` does not exist in `state.db` or in the pre-update snapshot.

### Impact

- **Data loss**: Full conversations conducted through the dashboard Chat tab are lost on any process restart
- **Desktop app blind spot**: The desktop app's sidebar reads from `state.db` and cannot see dashboard Chat tab sessions, even while they're live
- **No warning**: The user has no indication that their conversation isn't being persisted

### Additional context

The desktop app (`hermes desktop`) sidebar uses `/api/profiles/sessions` which reads from `state.db`. The dashboard's own session list appears to read from the TUI gateway's in-memory sessions, which is why the dashboard can show sessions the desktop app cannot. This discrepancy makes the issue hard to notice until the process is restarted.

The `_persist_session` / `_maybe_persist_session_row` code path in `tui_gateway/server.py` is supposed to fire on `prompt.submit` and write the session row via `db.create_session(...)`. Either this code path isn't being reached for dashboard Chat tab sessions, or it's failing silently (the `except Exception` block logs at debug level only).

items.title: [Bug] opencode-go: Qwen models fallback due to api_mode mismatch — /chat/completions instead of /messages

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When selecting a Qwen-series model (qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.7-max, qwen3.6-plus, qwen3.5-plus) from the opencode-go provider via `hermes model`, the agent calls `/chat/completions` instead of `/messages`, resulting in HTTP 500 → 3 retry failures → fallback to openrouter.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
hermes model  # opencode-go → qwen3.7-plus
# → Fallback activated: qwen3.7-plus → qwen/qwen3.7-plus (openrouter)
```

## Root Cause

OpenCode Go uses different API endpoints per model family:

| Model Family | Endpoint |
|-------------|----------|
| DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiMo | `/chat/completions` |
| **Qwen, MiniMax** | **`/messages`** (Anthropic Messages API) |

However, `hermes_cli/providers.py` L150-153 hardcodes the opencode-go provider transport as `openai_chat`:

```python
"opencode-go": HermesOverlay(
    transport="openai_chat",  # applied to ALL models, ignoring Qwen/MiniMax
    is_aggregator=True,
    base_url_env_var="OPENCODE_GO_BASE_URL",
),
```

The `determine_api_mode()` function (L542-581) decides `api_mode` at the provider level only — it never inspects the model name. `switch_model()` (agent_runtime_helpers.py L1772) has the same limitation. Qwen models are therefore called via `/chat/completions` → server returns 500 → fallback kicks in.

## Log Evidence

```
2026-07-13 10:35:50 model=qwen3.7-plus provider=opencode-go
2026-07-13 10:36:02 API call failed (attempt 1/3) HTTP 500: event:error
2026-07-13 10:36:15 API call failed (attempt 2/3) HTTP 500: event:error
2026-07-13 10:36:30 API call failed (attempt 3/3) HTTP 500: event:error
2026-07-13 10:36:30 Fallback activated: qwen3.7-plus → qwen/qwen3.7-plus (openrouter)
```

The `switch_model()` function (L1797-1803) already contains a defensive guard for opencode providers using `anthropic_messages`:

```python
if (
    api_mode == "anthropic_messages"
    and new_provider in {"opencode-zen", "opencode-go"}
    ...
):
    base_url = re.sub(r"/v1/?$", "", base_url)
```

This suggests the developers anticipated opencode-go + anthropic_messages — but the code path to reach `api_mode == "anthropic_messages"` is never triggered because `determine_api_mode()` always returns `chat_completions`.

## Core Issue

OpenCode Go is an aggregator where `/chat/completions` and `/messages` transports coexist within a single provider. Hermes' current `api_mode` resolution operates at the provider level only and cannot handle mixed-transport aggregators.

## Proposed Fixes

1. **Minimal**: Add a `model` parameter to `determine_api_mode()` and `switch_model()`, and detect Qwen/MiniMax model prefixes for opencode-go/openai providers → return `anthropic_messages`.
2. **Ideal**: Support per-model `api_mode` overrides in provider configuration — e.g. an optional `model_api_modes: {qwen3.7-plus: anthropic_messages}` field on `HermesOverlay` or in user config.

## Current Workaround

Route Qwen models through OpenRouter instead:

```bash
hermes config set model.default "qwen/qwen3.7-plus"
hermes config set model.provider openrouter
```

OpenRouter's `qwen/qwen3.7-plus` works correctly and is already confirmed via fallback logs.

## Environment

- Hermes: current main (2026-07-13)
- OS: macOS 26.5.2
- opencode-go base_url: `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`

labels.name: P1

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Summary

`GatewayRunner._drain_active_agents` (gateway/run.py, ~L5658 at 4281151ae) waits only on `self._running_agents` plus the cron scheduler's in-flight count. Agent runs served by the **api_server adapter** (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/runs` — i.e. every desktop-app/API client session) are tracked entirely inside the adapter (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`: `_inflight_agent_runs` at ~L903, `_active_run_agents` at ~L886) and are invisible to the drain.

Net effect: on any gateway stop/restart, desk/API sessions get **zero drain protection**. The drain logs `active_at_start=0` and "completes" in ~0.01s while api_server turns keep executing tool subprocesses; the process then survives until systemd's `TimeoutStopSec` SIGKILLs it (`Result=timeout`), killing tool work mid-flight with no warning.

### Observed

On a self-hosted 0.18.2 gateway (systemd user unit, Linux):

- A stop while two desktop sessions were mid-turn logged `drain took 0.01s … active_at_start=0`; both sessions kept running tools for ~2.5 more minutes until the unit's 210s stop-timeout SIGKILL (`Result=timeout`).
- A later restart drained 3m20s only because an *unrelated* wait; the in-flight api_server turn itself was never counted — it was interrupted mid-`hindsight_retain`.

### Why this is the same class as #60432

Cron jobs had exactly this structural blindness and were folded into the drain via `_active_cron_job_count()` (the comment block above the zero-work early return documents it). The api_server adapter needs the same fold-in.

### Suggested fix (patch running locally, happy to PR)

1. `APIServerAdapter.active_agent_work_count()` returning `self._inflight_agent_runs + len(self._active_run_agents)` (covers the non-streaming chat/responses paths and `/v1/runs` agents).
2. `GatewayRunner._active_api_run_count()` mirroring `_active_cron_job_count()` — best-effort, iterates `self.adapters` + `self._profile_adapters` for `Platform.API_SERVER` and sums the helper.
3. Fold it into `_drain_active_agents`: the zero-work early return, the wait-loop condition, the periodic status update, and the `timed_out` result.

Verified locally by binding the patched methods to a stub: zero-work still returns instantly; api_server work now blocks the drain until it finishes or the timeout fires.

Related but separate: at drain timeout, `_interrupt_running_agents` also only reaches `self._running_agents`, so api_server runs aren't interrupted gracefully either — the fold-in above at least gives them the full drain window instead of an instant kill.

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

# Summary
The Slack adapter decides whether an un-mentioned message in a non-free-response channel should be processed via three checks (plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py on current main, ~line 2852; gateway/platforms/slack.py ~line 2323 in 0.16.0):

thread root ts ∈ _bot_message_ts — populated only by the adapter’s own send() path (and, on main, files_upload_v2)
thread ts ∈ _mentioned_threads — populated on @mention
_has_active_session_for_thread(...) — the only check that survives restarts
This leaves two gaps (both still present on main as of v2026.7.7.2):

## Gap A: messages posted outside gateway send() are invisible
Agents commonly post to Slack via the Web API directly (chat.postMessage with the same bot token) — e.g. from skills/scripts that need Block Kit formatting, thread_ts targeting of threads created by other bots (incident alert threads), or cron data-collection scripts that post without an agent run. The gateway has no record of these messages, so a human replying in-thread (without @-mentioning the bot) is silently dropped. From the user’s perspective the bot started a conversation and then ignores the answer.

Concrete case: an on-call watcher posts triage analysis into [incident.io](http://incident.io/) alert threads; engineers reply in-thread with follow-up questions; the agent never wakes. (The gateway’s own send_message can’t be used here because the thread parent belongs to another bot and isn’t resolvable by the gateway, so it falls back to channel root.)

## Gap B: _bot_message_ts / _mentioned_threads are in-memory only
Both sets are wiped on gateway restart. After a pod restart, threads where the bot was previously conversing stop waking it unless an agent session happened to exist for that exact thread key (check 3). Messages delivered via send_message/cron deliver to a channel (no session) lose reply-tracking entirely on restart.

# Environment
hermes-agent 0.16.0 (docker nousresearch/hermes-agent, GKE deployment); gaps re-verified against main @ v2026.7.7.2 (plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py)
Slack adapter via socket mode, require_mention: true, no free-response channels

#38861 is adjacent (bot’s own replies filtered from cold-start thread context) but distinct: that issue is about context content once the agent wakes; this one is about the agent never waking at all.
#51019 touches the same sets (eviction order) but not the wake gap.

For Gap A: when an un-mentioned thread reply fails checks 1–3, fall back to fetching the thread root via conversations.replies and checking whether the bot authored the root (or participated in the thread). labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

`state.db` gets corrupted daily on macOS with `btreeInitPage() returns error code 11` across dozens of btree pages. The corruption occurs during early morning hours, triggered by a WAL checkpoint race with process termination.

## Root Cause

`hermes_state.py:366-372`, function `apply_wal_with_fallback()`:

```python
if current_mode and current_mode[0] == "wal":
    _apply_macos_checkpoint_barrier(conn)
    return "wal"  # ← Skips setting synchronous=FULL!
```

When a DB is already in WAL mode, the function **skips setting `synchronous=FULL`**, leaving it at the default `synchronous=NORMAL` (value 1). On macOS this is unsafe because Apples `fsync()` does not guarantee data-on-platter (documented Darwin behavior).

During a WAL checkpoint:
1. WAL frames are merged into the main DB
2. Only `fsync()` is called (not `F_FULLFSYNC`)
3. If the process is killed before pages actually hit the platter
4. Main DB ends up with half-written btree pages → `btreeInitPage error 11`

The corruption is on btree pages, not FTS indexes, meaning `repair_state_db_schema()` (which handles FTS-level corruption) cannot fix it — it returns `"database disk image is malformed"` and falls back to backup restore.

## Fix Applied (local)

```python
if current_mode and current_mode[0] == "wal":
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=FULL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA fullfsync=ON")
    _apply_macos_checkpoint_barrier(conn)
    return "wal"
```

`PRAGMA fullfsync=ON` forces `F_FULLFSYNC` on macOS — the only syscall that guarantees data durability.

## Expected Fix in Code

`apply_wal_with_fallback()` should always enforce `synchronous=FULL` + `fullfsync=ON` on Darwin, regardless of whether WAL was already set from a previous connection.

## Environment

- macOS 26.5.1
- Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)
- Filesystem: APFS (internal SSD), no NFS/SMB

items.body:
Currently, two types of Hermes system status messages leak into user-facing chat channels (LINE, Telegram, etc.) with no config switch to disable them:

1. `⏳ Working — X min — iteration N/150, waiting for provider response (streaming)`
   Shown while the agent is waiting for the LLM provider to stream a response.

2. `💾 Self-improvement review: Skill 'X' created.`
   Shown every time Hermes automatically creates or patches a skill during a session.

Both messages are internal status updates that end users should not see. Similar noise is already suppressible via existing flags (`display.tool_progress: false`, `credits_notices: false`), but these two remain unconfigurable.

**Proposed fix:**
- Add a boolean config flag, e.g. `system_status_notices: false`
- When disabled, suppress both the streaming "Working" wait notice and the "Self-improvement review" skill-creation notice from chat output
- Keep the underlying behaviors unchanged; only hide the status strings sent to messaging adapters

**Context:**
Hermes is used as a customer-facing bot on LINE. End users see these system strings in the same thread as business replies, harming UX.
